title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Discover the functional study hubs, specialized labs, and quiet corners that Brown University students use for daily academic life beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: Friedman Study Center
cards.subtitle: Sciences Library Level A
cards.notes: Access this 24-hour hub on Level A of the SciLi for collaborative work, featuring group study rooms and over 65 computer workstations.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour collaborative study hub located at the base of the Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Friedman Study Center is a 24-hour space on Level A of the Sciences Library with 8 private group study rooms and 65+ computer workstations.
cards.source_title: Friedman Study Center - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for students with Brown ID swipe access.

cards.title: Willis Reading Room
cards.subtitle: John Hay Library
cards.notes: Study in this grand, quiet space within the special collections library, known for its historic atmosphere and rare book surroundings.
cards.short_summary: A historic and quiet reading room located within the John Hay Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Willis Reading Room is a primary study space located in the John Hay Library, which houses rare books and university archives.
cards.source_title: John Hay Library Home Page - Brown University Library
cards.access_notes: Open to current Brown students, faculty, and staff; check library hours for public access times.

cards.title: The Sunlab
cards.subtitle: CIT Building Room 143
cards.notes: Utilize this primary computing facility for CS students, featuring 73 Linux workstations and 24-hour access during peak times.
cards.short_summary: The main undergraduate computer science lab located in the CIT building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sunlab (CIT 143) is the primary computing resource for computer science undergraduates, featuring 73 PCs running Linux.
cards.access_notes: Available days and evenings; 24-hour access often available for CS students.

cards.title: Global Brown Lounge
cards.subtitle: Page-Robinson Hall Room 310
cards.notes: Visit 'The Globe' for a dedicated community space supporting international students and global learning initiatives.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge for Brown's international community in Page-Robinson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Global Brown Lounge, or 'The Globe', is located in Page-Robinson Hall room 310 and is open to the community from 9am to 5pm.
cards.access_notes: Open 9am-5pm for all; after-hours access available for international students via request.

cards.title: Granoff Multimedia Lab
cards.subtitle: Granoff Center for the Creative Arts
cards.notes: Explore this lab for electronics prototyping, sensor interface development, and physical computing projects.
cards.short_summary: A specialized lab for multimedia and physical computing in the Granoff Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Granoff Center features a multimedia lab and physical media lab supporting electronics prototyping and physical computing.
cards.source_title: The Perry and Marty Granoff Center for the Creative Arts | Brown Arts Institute
cards.access_notes: Building hours vary by season; typically open to students during academic terms.

cards.title: Wernig Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Rockefeller Library 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this dedicated area featuring a kitchen, eating space, and seminar rooms for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading room and lounge for graduate students in the Rockefeller Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wernig Graduate Student Reading Room is on the 2nd floor of the Rockefeller Library and includes a study area, kitchen, and seminar room.
cards.source_title: Wernig Reading Room | Graduate Student Council - Brown University
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate students with Brown ID swipe access.

cards.title: SciLi Meditation Room
cards.subtitle: Sciences Library Room 1219
cards.notes: Find a moment of quiet in this dedicated meditation space; check out the room key from the Level A service desk.
cards.short_summary: A quiet meditation space located on the 12th floor of the Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: A meditation room (1219) is located on Level 12 of the Sciences Library; keys are available at the Level A service desk.
cards.source_title: Sciences Library Stack Guide and Services
cards.access_notes: Key checkout required at the Level A service desk.

cards.title: List Art Student Galleries
cards.subtitle: List Art Building
cards.notes: View rotating exhibitions of student work in these galleries, which host senior capstone shows during the spring semester.
cards.short_summary: Exhibition spaces in the List Art Building dedicated to displaying student artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: The List Art Building houses exhibition spaces primarily dedicated to the display of student work, including Senior Capstone Exhibitions.
cards.source_title: Student Exhibitions and Guidelines | Visual Art | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours: 8:30am-5:00pm during the academic year.

cards.title: Campus Center Lounges
cards.subtitle: Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center
cards.notes: Use these common rooms for impromptu meetings or study sessions in the heart of campus life at Faunce House.
cards.short_summary: Common lounge and meeting spaces available for student use in the Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center (Faunce House) offers common spaces for impromptu meetings and study use.
cards.source_title: Stephen Robert '62 Campus Center - Student Activities | Brown University
cards.access_notes: Open to all university community members during building hours.

cards.title: Nightingale-Brown House Grounds
cards.subtitle: 357 Benefit Street
cards.notes: Walk through the historic gardens designed by Frederick Law Olmsted at this landmark home, now used for public humanities.
cards.short_summary: Historic grounds and gardens of the Nightingale-Brown House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nightingale-Brown House grounds include a garden designed by Frederick Law Olmsted in 1890.
cards.source_title: Nightingale-Brown House History | John Nicholas Brown Center
cards.access_notes: Grounds are generally accessible; building use is for faculty, students, and staff of the Center.
